title: Introduction
description: Follow a request from local capture to useful evidence.
text:
Follow the request.

Snurpo is a desktop HTTP(S) debugger with a curious nose and a local archive. Route a request through it, inspect what happened, change the next exchange, and keep the evidence for later.

Capture, saved sessions, export and built-in analysis work without an account or subscription. Your application still contacts its normal servers. Connecting an external MCP client is a separate, explicit choice.

   Get a useful result first

1.  Install Snurpo (installation.md) for your operating system.
2.  Capture the included local traffic (first-capture.md). No phone or certificate setup is needed.
3. Pick a request and inspect its response, headers and timing.
4.  Replay it or copy a cURL command (replay-curl.md), then compare the result.

! Snurpo's native traffic inspector showing captured requests and response details. (/assets/traffic-inspector.webp)

This native screenshot records Snurpo 1.4.2. The guides describe 1.5.0, which adds Copy as cURL.

   Choose the next question

  What are you investigating?   Start here  
  ---   ---  
  What did my app send?    Inspect and search (inspect-and-search.md)  
  Why is HTTPS failing?    HTTPS and certificate trust (https.md)  
  What happens if the API returns an error?    Rules and breakpoints (rules-breakpoints.md)  
  What changed between two captures?    Analysis and comparison (analysis.md)  
  Can my agent inspect this evidence?    MCP access (mcp.md)  
  Can I capture an Android app?    Experimental Android workflows (android.md)  
  Can this become a CI check?    Offline HAR comparison (har-compare-ci.md)  

   Know what you are looking at

A mock is labeled as a mock. Edited messages retain originals. A replay creates a new exchange. These distinctions matter when you explain a failure or share a report.

Snurpo currently buffers bodies up to 16 MiB each. It does not implement streaming capture, WebSocket frames, HTTP trailers or HTTP/3. Observed API schemas describe your sample; they are not a complete contract.

Snurpo was previously called Scope. Some file names and MCP identifiers remain compatible by design.  Release and migration notes (releases.md) explain what stays the same.

title: Install Snurpo
description: Choose a verified release asset and understand platform support.
text:
Install Snurpo

Download Snurpo 1.5.0 from the  published GitHub release (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/tag/v1.5.0). The desktop packages include the capture engine and companion MCP executable. Node.js, Rust and a model account are not required to run them.

   Choose your download

  Computer   Package  
  ---   ---  
  macOS, Apple Silicon    Snurpo-v1.5.0-macOS-arm64.zip (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/download/v1.5.0/Snurpo-v1.5.0-macOS-arm64.zip)  
  Windows, x64    Snurpo-v1.5.0-Windows-x64-setup.exe (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/download/v1.5.0/Snurpo-v1.5.0-Windows-x64-setup.exe)  
  Linux, x64    AppImage (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/download/v1.5.0/Snurpo-v1.5.0-Linux-x64.AppImage) or  Debian package (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/download/v1.5.0/Snurpo-v1.5.0-Linux-x64.deb)  

There is no Intel macOS or Linux arm64 package in this release. Windows and Linux packages have CI build and headless protocol coverage; interactive installers, desktop use and device behavior on those hosts remain unverified. Native interaction has been exercised on macOS Apple Silicon.

   Verify and open

Compare your file's SHA-256 with  SHA256SUMS.txt (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/download/v1.5.0/SHA256SUMS.txt). For example, on macOS:

 

On Windows, use  Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256  in PowerShell; on Linux, use  sha256sum .

On macOS, extract the ZIP, move   Snurpo.app   into Applications and open it. The app is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. After verifying the download, use   System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway   if macOS blocks the first launch. Keep Gatekeeper enabled.

On Windows, run the x64 installer. On Linux, use the package appropriate for your distribution. An AppImage needs executable permission:

 

Linux has a tracked glib dependency advisory; see the  dependency record (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md) for its status and boundaries.

   Updating an existing installation

Quit the old app before opening the new one. Scope and Snurpo share the same archive and CA; do not run both at once or rename their data files. Back up important captures before an upgrade.  Compatibility details (releases.md).

Optional Frida binaries are not bundled. You only need them for the  Frida Android workflow (android.md), not ordinary desktop capture.

Continue with  your first capture (first-capture.md).

title: Your first capture
description: Capture six real localhost requests, then connect your own client.
text:
Catch your first request

The fastest way to learn Snurpo is its built-in local fixture. It sends real requests through the capture engine, so you can inspect the whole path without configuring another app.

   Try the local traffic

1. Open the native Snurpo app.
2. Select   Generate test traffic   in the empty inspector, or the lightning bolt beside   New session  . Its tooltip is   Generate real test traffic through the proxy  .
3. Select a captured row. Switch between   Request   and   Response  , then   Body  ,   Headers   and   Timing  .
4. Open   Analysis  . Follow an observation using   Inspect a request  .
5. Select   Stop capture  , quit Snurpo and reopen it. The saved session remains available.

The fixture runs on  127.0.0.1:17891  and sends six requests through the proxy, normally  127.0.0.1:17890 . It includes an intentional sign-in failure, repeated product calls and a slow endpoint. An HTTP 401 in this fixture is expected.

If a matching pause rule or global breakpoint is enabled, disable it before generating the automatic batch. Use your own client when you want to  pause a request interactively (rules-breakpoints.md).

   Connect your own client

Create a session with   New session  , then select   Start capture  .   Connection settings   shows the current listener address and port. Configure your HTTP client to use that proxy:

 

This command sends a real request to example.com. Replace the proxy port if you changed it in Snurpo. The listener binds to localhost; it is not a proxy exposed to your whole network.

Select the new exchange and compare what your client sent with what the server returned. For encrypted traffic, continue with  HTTPS setup (https.md).

   Keep the investigation readable

Use   Session details   beside the session name to add a useful name, notes, tags or a pin. Capture is autosaved in the local archive.   Stop capture   stops listening; it does not delete the session.

Next:  find related requests (inspect-and-search.md),  replay one (replay-curl.md), or  export the session (sessions-export.md).

title: HTTPS and trust
description: Configure the proxy and trust its public CA in a test client.
text:
Inspect HTTPS

HTTPS inspection needs two things: your client must route through Snurpo, and it must trust Snurpo's local certificate authority. A proxy setting alone is not enough.

   Connect a test client

1. Create or select a session and start capture.
2. Open   Connection settings  .
3. Under   Certificate authority  , use   Copy certificate path  .
4. Configure your client to trust that public certificate and use the displayed proxy address.

For cURL, replace the certificate placeholder with the actual copied path:

 

The path is installation-specific. Keep it quoted if it contains spaces. TLS verification remains enabled;  --insecure  is not part of this setup.

   Public certificate, private signing key

Snurpo creates a local CA and keeps its signing key in the application data directory. Configure clients with the public  scope-ca.pem  certificate only. Do not distribute  scope-ca-key.pem  or include it in a bug report.

These legacy names are intentional compatibility identifiers. An existing CA can also display   Scope Local Debug CA  . Updating to Snurpo does not require deleting or regenerating it.

   When trust is not enough

An application can ignore the system proxy, use its own trust store, enforce certificate pinning, or send traffic over an unsupported protocol. An empty capture does not prove that the application made no request.

  Symptom   Check  
  ---   ---  
  No exchange appears   Confirm the client actually uses the configured HTTP proxy.  
  Certificate validation fails   Check the copied CA path and the client's selected trust store.  
  cURL works but an app fails   Check app-specific trust, pinning and networking stack.  
  An Android app rejects HTTPS   Follow the  Android guide (android.md); system proxy mode does not install a system CA or bypass pinning.  

Snurpo currently does not support HTTP/3 or WebSocket frame inspection. Use  troubleshooting (troubleshooting.md) to separate connection, trust and capture problems.

title: Inspect and search
description: Read messages and combine filters across a saved session.
text:
Find the interesting request

Select a session, then pick a row in the traffic table.   Request   and   Response   select a message;   Body  ,   Headers   and   Timing   show its details. An edited exchange also exposes   Original  .

Repeated headers remain separate entries. Mocked and blocked responses carry their provenance, and applied rules are listed in the inspector. A pending exchange is not automatically a failed exchange.

   Search the whole selected session

An ordinary query is a case-insensitive substring across method, URL, status, headers and stored bodies. Spaces remain part of that substring.

Use the exact lowercase prefix  filter:  to combine structured conditions:

 

All conditions must match the same exchange.   Search syntax   under the field offers clickable examples.

  Field   Supported operators   Meaning  
  ---   ---   ---  
   method     = ,  !=    Exact method, ignoring ASCII case.  
   host     = ,  !=    Exact hostname without port, ignoring case.  
   status     = ,  != ,  > ,  >= ,  < ,  <=    HTTP status from 100 to 599.  
   body     ~=    Substring in plain request or response bodies; excludes base64 bodies.  
   state     =     pending ,  error  or  complete .  
   edited     =     true  or  false .  

Quote values containing spaces. Inside quotes,  \"  represents a quote and  \\  a backslash. There is no OR, regex or nested-expression syntax. Invalid queries show an error rather than silently becoming a successful empty search.

 state=error  means a completed exchange with a recorded error or HTTP status at least 400.  state=complete  excludes those errors. A missing status matches none of the status operators, including  != .

   Two filters, different reach

Structured conditions apply before pagination across the selected archive session. The   All traffic / Successful / Errors / Edited   dropdown filters the currently returned page.

To search literal text beginning with a reserved prefix, use:

 

Structured queries are limited to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and 32 conditions. Search still scans saved records; it is not a large-session indexing feature. MCP search has a separate sanitized view and does not accept this structured grammar.  MCP details (mcp.md).

title: Rules and breakpoints
description: Mock, rewrite, block or pause an intended request.
text:
Change the next exchange

Open   Traffic rules   and select   New rule  . A rule can rewrite a request or response, return a mock, block a request, or pause a real message for editing. Rules are saved locally and affect all capture sessions.

   Make a local maintenance response

After generating the  local fixture (first-capture.md), create this rule in the editor:

  Field   Value  
  ---   ---  
  Method    GET   
  Host    127.0.0.1   
  Path starts with    /api/products   
  Action     Mock response    
  Status    503   
  Header    Content-Type: application/json   
  Body    {"maintenance":true}   

Save and enable the rule, then send a new matching request. The inspector marks the result   Mock response  . A mock does not contact the upstream server. Disable the rule when the experiment is finished.

   Pause an endpoint

1. Match the intended host and path, then choose   Pause & edit  .
2. Under   Pause at  , choose request, response or both. Save and enable the rule.
3. Send a request through the proxy from your client.
4. Open the paused-message banner. The editor contains the actual message.
5. Edit and continue it, continue unchanged, or abort the transfer.

Request pauses happen before upstream delivery. Response pauses hold the result before your client receives it. Both creates a separate pause for each stage.

> A pause expires after 60 seconds and aborts the transfer. Closing the editor does not release it. Your client's own timeout may be shorter.

The global Request/Response breakpoint buttons pause all proxied messages when enabled. Endpoint pause rules only affect their matches. Stopping capture aborts outstanding pauses.

   Matching and ordering

Matchers are ANDed: exact method, exact host without port, path prefix and URL substring. Lower priority numbers run first, then rule ID. The request keeps the enabled-rule snapshot and original matching result from its entry point.

Automatic edits run before manual pauses. A terminal mock or block stops later request actions, but matched response rewrites and pauses can still apply.   Replay   uses current automatic rules and skips manual breakpoints.

Replacing headers replaces the complete list. Changing a destination can forward existing credentials there, so review the whole request. Rule bodies are limited to 1 MiB, independently of the 16 MiB capture limit.

See the  complete rule schema and ordering reference (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/RULES.md) for programmatic configuration and downgrade compatibility.

title: Replay and cURL
description: Send an edited replay or preview a complete terminal command.
text:
Send it again, deliberately

Snurpo offers two ways to reuse a captured request.   Compose replay   sends a new exchange from Snurpo.   Copy as cURL   prepares a command for your terminal. Opening either editor does not send the request.

   Compose a replay

1. Select the captured exchange and choose   Compose replay  .
2. Review the method,   Request URL  , complete header list and body.
3. Use   Binary as base64   when editing binary body data.
4. Choose   Send request   to send it and record a new exchange.

The original capture remains available, and the replay is recorded in its original session. Current automatic traffic rules apply; manual breakpoints are skipped. To pause a message, send it through the proxy from your test client instead.

Native replay keeps TLS verification enabled, does not follow redirects and ignores environment proxy variables. Its transport timeout is 120 seconds. A timeout does not prove that the upstream server did not perform a write.

Captured authorization headers and cookies are reused unless you change them. If you change the destination, check those headers before sending.

   Copy as cURL in 1.5.0

Select   Copy as cURL  , review the command, then choose   Copy command  . If clipboard access fails, select and copy the preview text manually.

The command targets a POSIX shell such as sh, bash or zsh. On Windows, use WSL or another compatible shell; PowerShell and cmd.exe syntax are not generated.

Copying sends no traffic. Running the command sends a real request with your terminal's network settings. Snurpo rules and breakpoints are not applied. TLS verification stays enabled, cURL's configuration file is disabled, and no automatic redirects or retries are added. Terminal proxy environment variables can still apply.

   What the command preserves

The export uses the effective captured request, including repeated end-to-end headers and text or binary body bytes. It does not export the pre-rewrite original as a wire recording.

Host, Content-Length and hop-by-hop headers are normalized for the new transport. Proxy credentials and host overrides are not reproduced. Whitespace-only header values are normalized to empty values.

> The command contains the captured URL, headers and body, including credentials. It is a debugging export, not a sanitized sharing copy.

Malformed inputs, HEAD requests with a body, more than 1,024 input headers or a command reaching 128 KiB produce an explanation instead of a partial command. Use replay or  session export (sessions-export.md) when cURL export is unsuitable.

title: Sessions and exports
description: Organize, import and export evidence with an explicit content policy.
text:
Keep the evidence

Snurpo saves captured exchanges to its local SQLite archive. Stopping capture or reopening the app does not erase the session.   Connection settings > Session archive   shows the actual data directory.

   Organize a session

Open   Session details   beside the session name. Give the investigation a name, add notes and comma-separated tags, or pin it for quick access.

Deleting a session is a separate confirmation that requires its name. It removes captured messages and notes. Export a copy first if you need to keep the evidence; an active capture cannot be deleted.

   Choose an export

Open   Export  , select the content policy, then the format:

  Format   Use it for  
  ---   ---  
    HAR archive     Moving HTTP evidence to other tools or the offline comparison CLI.  
    Snurpo session     Preserving native session information, including originals and edits when retained by the content policy.  
    Observed OpenAPI     Exploring the API shape visible in this session.  

  Sanitized   is selected by default in the desktop export menu. It masks recognized credential fields and creates a lossy sharing copy.   Raw capture   retains captured headers and bodies, including credentials. Review custom fields in either case before sharing.

The native format still uses  .scope.json  and compatibility identifiers from earlier releases. Do not rename internal schema keys to match the product name.

   Import and compare

Choose   Import session or HAR   in the sidebar and select the archive. Snurpo opens the imported session so you can inspect it or select it under   Compare sessions  .

HAR tools differ in what they capture. Missing bodies, timings or original-message details cannot be reconstructed by importing the file. Compare observations with that limitation in mind.

   Back up useful work

Use a raw native export when you need to preserve a private investigation, and keep that file private. For a complete application-data backup, stop capture and quit Snurpo first; the directory also contains sensitive CA and bridge material.

Records currently load into memory. Large-capture streaming import and export are not implemented. Bodies are limited to 16 MiB each. Keep investigations focused instead of assuming an unlimited archive can be opened cheaply.

Next:  understand a session (analysis.md) or  compare HARs in CI (har-compare-ci.md).

title: Analysis and comparison
description: Explore observed endpoints, compare captures and infer an API shape.
text:
Turn traffic into a lead

Select a captured or imported session and open   Analysis  . Snurpo computes observations locally, without sending the capture to a model or requiring an account.

   Read the session summary

The view shows request count, average duration, error count and total traffic. The   Endpoint map   groups observed endpoints with their request counts, errors, average time and volume. Request counts can include saved in-flight exchanges; timing and error observations use completed exchanges.

An insight can link back to evidence with   Inspect a request  . Use that exchange to check the body, timing, provenance and applied rules before deciding what caused a problem.

Repeated calls can be intentional. Recorded duration includes breakpoint waiting and body buffering, so it is not pure server latency. Mocked or blocked responses must be distinguished from upstream behavior.

   Compare two sessions

1. Select the baseline session in the sidebar.
2. Open   Compare sessions  .
3. Choose another saved session under   Compare with  .
4. Select   Compare  .

The comparison reports added, removed and changed observed endpoints, with status, timing and JSON-field differences where available. Imported sessions can participate too. Desktop grouping uses method, hostname and a normalized path, replacing numeric or UUID segments with  :id ; query, scheme and port do not separate those groups.

Capture comparable user flows when possible. A different page, account state or sequence of actions can change the sample even when the application code is unchanged. This desktop comparison is distinct from the stricter operation matching and authored contracts in the HAR CLI.

   Explore an observed API

Choose   Export > Observed OpenAPI   to infer an OpenAPI 3.1.1 document from the selected session. The result describes observed endpoints and bounded schemas; it does not infer required fields, authentication, enums, constraints or unseen responses. It can include synthetic responses with separate evidence counts.

Observed schemas are not authored requirements. If CI must reject a missing required field or an unchanged HTTP 500, write an explicit assertion in the separate  HAR comparison workflow (har-compare-ci.md).

An MCP client can request the same local analyses after you  share the relevant sessions (mcp.md). Its interpretation is separate from Snurpo's recorded observations.

title: Connect an MCP client
description: Share selected evidence through stdio with separate write permissions.
text:
Let your agent follow the evidence

Snurpo exposes selected captured sessions through a local stdio MCP server. The desktop app controls access. This is separate from Plompy's HTTP integration gateway: Snurpo does not offer a remote MCP URL to paste into that configuration.

   Connect a client

1. Open Snurpo and select a session.
2. Open   MCP server   and enable   Share selected session with MCP  .
3. Use   Copy config   under   Client configuration  .
4. Merge that configuration into a compatible client's settings and reconnect it.
5. Keep Snurpo open. Ask the client to call  status , then  list_sessions .

Use the generated paths from your installation. The configuration has this shape:

 

 scope-mcp  and the existing  scope  entry are retained for compatibility. On Windows the executable uses  .exe . Adapt the outer configuration shape to your client without changing these actual paths.

The internal localhost bridge is not a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint. Do not substitute  http://127.0.0.1:17892/api  for the stdio command.

   Grant only the access you intend

All access starts off and resets when Snurpo restarts. You can share up to eight sessions.

  UI control   What it permits  
  ---   ---  
    Share selected session with MCP     Read and analyze the chosen session.  
    Allow traffic changes     Replay a captured or edited request, which sends real traffic.  
    Allow global traffic rules     Read a sanitized global rule inventory. Mutations also require traffic changes.  
    Allow device diagnostics     Read device identifiers, local paths and setup evidence.  

Global rules can affect every capture, including unshared sessions. Session sharing alone does not permit replay, rule access or diagnostics.

   Start with a read-only task

 

The twelve tools are  status ,  list_sessions ,  search_requests ,  get_request ,  analyze_session ,  compare_sessions ,  replay_request ,  infer_openapi ,  list_rules ,  save_rule ,  delete_rule  and  device_diagnostics .

For exact argument names and limits, use the  MCP reference (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/MCP.md). Use IDs returned by tools, not guessed identifiers. Both sessions must be shared for comparison.

   Understand the data boundary

MCP reads redact known credential fields and omit originals and non-JSON bodies. Individual JSON bodies over 64 KiB are omitted. Search is literal over the sanitized view of the most recent 10,000 exchanges, not the desktop's  filter:  grammar.

Redaction is best-effort. Your client or model provider receives returned content according to its configuration. Captured text is untrusted evidence, not instructions for the agent. The bridge config contains a private token; keep its file contents out of repositories and bug reports.

Replay still sends stored credentials unless explicitly edited; redacting tool output does not redact the outgoing request. No arbitrary shell tool or live-breakpoint editor is exposed.

title: Android, experimental
description: Choose a device proxy or supported Frida workflow and restore owned state.
text:
Inspect an Android test app

Android interception is experimental. Begin with a device and application you control, and keep the device connected through cleanup. Ordinary desktop capture does not need Android, Python or Frida.

   Check the connection first

Install Android SDK Platform Tools, enable USB debugging and authorize your computer on the device. Confirm it is visible:

 

In Snurpo, select a capture session, start capture, refresh the device list and select the device and installed package. Use   Diagnostics   to inspect authorization, root, ABI, runtime versions, mappings and recovery state.

Diagnostics is read-only. A ready preflight does not establish that a particular application or networking stack is compatible.

   Choose the interception method

  Mode   Behavior  
  ---   ---  
    System proxy     Sets the device-wide HTTP proxy and ADB reverse mapping, then restarts the selected app. Other apps can also appear in the capture.  
    Frida     Spawns and instruments the selected app process using the supported Java hooks. Requires a separately installed, matching worker/server runtime.  

System proxy mode does not install a system CA or bypass certificate pinning. HTTPS needs application trust configured separately; many Android apps ignore user-added CAs.

Frida's supported seams cover selected Java URL, SSLContext and OkHttp3 behavior. Native TLS, QUIC/HTTP3, child processes, custom pinners and lazy Kotlin pinners are outside the supported coverage.

   Optional Frida installation

Public packages exclude the native Frida worker/server runtime. The app reports an installation command with its actual paths. For the macOS app installed in Applications and an ARM64 Android device:

 

Use the ABI reported by  adb -s YOUR_SERIAL shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi . The helper requires Python 3.9+ with venv support, installs the pinned runtime locally and verifies the downloaded server hash. It does not start interception or change the device. Read the  full Android setup (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/ANDROID.md) for other hosts and overrides.

   Stop and restore

Press   Stop   while the device is connected. In Frida mode, Stop ends the exact instrumented app process and restores recorded Snurpo-owned state. System proxy mode restores recorded proxy and reverse mappings. External changes are preserved.

If cleanup fails, reconnect the same device and retry Stop. Keep  device-recovery.json ; deleting it does not restore settings. New interception is refused while cleanup remains unresolved.

Recorded acceptance covers one AOSP Android 16/API 36 ARM64 setup with Frida 17.9.1 and OkHttp 3.14.9. Other OS/ABI combinations, physical devices and active-worker crash/restart recovery remain unverified.  Detailed acceptance evidence (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/ANDROID_ACCEPTANCE.md).

title: HAR comparison and CI
description: Compare saved HARs offline and interpret clean, regression and invalid results.
text:
Check saved HARs offline

Snurpo includes a separate dependency-free Node CLI for comparing two saved HAR captures. It does not open the desktop, replay requests, call a model or upload the captures. This remains a local CI experiment, with its own version  0.1.0 .

   Run a comparison

Use a Snurpo source checkout and Node.js 26.13.1 or newer. No npm install is needed for the CLI itself. From the repository root:

 

Supply captures you already saved. Output paths must be new and distinct; existing files are not overwritten. The CLI also writes analysis JSON to stdout, so choose where your shell or CI retains it.

  Exit code   Meaning  
  ---   ---  
   0    Analysis completed with no configured regression candidates. Informational findings may remain.  
   1    Completed analysis found regression candidates; reports are available.  
   2    Invalid input, configuration, output or incomplete analysis. This is not a clean result.  

The default  shape  mode detects changes such as removed observed JSON fields and changed types.  strict  also checks scalar value changes. Repeated matching requests pair in HAR encounter order; this is a deterministic assumption, not proof that two operations mean the same thing.

   Express a requirement explicitly

An unchanged HTTP 500 does not fail merely because it is an error. A change detector needs an authored requirement to reject that case. For example, save this as  contract.json :

 

Pass  --config contract.json  and substitute your actual operation. Unsupported or missing selected response bodies fail analysis rather than being silently skipped. Mixed browser HARs often need explicit operation selection.

   Use the GitHub Action

The repository's composite Action wraps the same CLI on Linux. The caller supplies Node 26.13.1+, Bash and the capture files. A step can use:

 

Pin an inspected full commit SHA for a stable dependency. The output directory must not exist. The default gate fails on either  1  or  2 ; deferred gating requires your own final check that also rejects a missing result.

Neither the CLI nor the Action automatically uploads artifacts.  labels: ids  removes captured labels from reports but does not guarantee anonymity. Review reports before sharing them.

See the  CLI reference (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/tools/har-compare/README.md) for matching and selection limits, and the  Action reference (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/.github/actions/har-compare/README.md) for a complete workflow and output contract.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Identify the failing connection, trust, capture or permission step.
text:
Find the failing step

Separate the desktop, proxy, client trust and captured evidence. A visible window does not mean a client is using the proxy, and a running listener does not prove that an app accepts the CA.

   Start with a local control

Try   Generate test traffic  . If six loopback requests appear, inspect one response and reopen the saved session. That gives you a working desktop/proxy/archive path before adding HTTPS or a device.

  Symptom   Next check  
  ---   ---  
  Port is busy   Check for another Snurpo or old Scope instance. Default ports are 17890 for the proxy, 17891 for the local fixture and 17892 for the internal bridge.  
  Local fixture works, my app is absent   Confirm the app uses the displayed HTTP proxy. Check its networking stack and protocol.  
  HTTPS fails   Verify the CA path and client trust, then investigate pinning separately.  HTTPS guide (https.md).  
  Paused transfer fails   Check the 60-second breakpoint expiry and the client's shorter timeout. Closing the editor does not continue traffic.  
  Demo generation refuses to run   Disable global breakpoints and matching pause rules; stop an active capture in another session.  
  Structured search is empty   Check the exact lowercase  filter:  prefix and supported fields. A malformed query produces an error.  
  MCP cannot see a session   Share it in   MCP server  . Sharing resets after desktop restart.  
  MCP body is omitted   Non-JSON, oversized and original snapshots have deliberate output limits. Inspect the raw message locally.  
  Browser preview cannot capture    npm run dev  is a frontend preview. Use the installed app or  npm run desktop .  
  cURL preview cannot be generated   Read the displayed validation error. Try replay or export for oversized or unsupported requests.  

Do not stop unrelated processes simply because a port is occupied.   Connection settings   lets you change the proxy port while capture is stopped; update your client to match.

   Android cleanup

Use   Diagnostics   before interception. If a device disconnects during cleanup, reconnect the same device and press   Stop   again. Preserve recovery state until restoration succeeds. The  Android guide (android.md) explains mode-specific behavior and unsupported combinations.

   Report a reproducible problem

Use the  issue forms (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/issues/new/choose). Include the Snurpo version, OS/architecture, exact action, expected result and observed error. If possible, reproduce it with local synthetic traffic.

Review attached captures and logs first. Leave out private CA keys, bridge tokens, account cookies and raw authorization headers. Sanitized exports mask known fields but still need review. Screenshot the relevant app area without unrelated desktop overlays or cursor highlights.

For release-specific limitations, see  releases and compatibility (releases.md).

title: Releases and compatibility
description: Understand version 1.5.0, tested platforms and preserved Scope identifiers.
text:
Releases and compatibility

These guides describe   Snurpo 1.5.0  , published on 12 November 2026. Use the  release page (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases/tag/v1.5.0) for downloads and checksums, or  all releases (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/releases) for the full history.

   What 1.5.0 adds

  Copy as cURL   carries an effective captured request into a POSIX terminal. You preview it before copying; neither action sends traffic. Repeated headers and text or binary bodies are supported within the documented limits.  Usage and boundaries (replay-curl.md).

The installed desktop app needs no Node runtime. Source tooling requires Node 26.13.1 or newer. The separate HAR comparison CLI keeps its own  0.1.0  version.

   Download availability and validation

  Target   Current evidence  
  ---   ---  
  macOS Apple Silicon   Native interaction has been exercised. Public ZIP is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized.  
  Windows x64   Installer available; CI build/package and headless MCP/capture coverage. Interactive use remains unverified.  
  Linux x64   AppImage and Debian package available; CI build/package and headless MCP/capture coverage. Interactive use remains unverified.  
  Intel macOS / Linux arm64   No package in the 1.5.0 release.  
  Android / Frida   Experimental coverage for the specific setup described in the  Android guide (android.md).  

The gallery's existing native screenshots record   1.4.2  . They are not screenshots of the 1.5.0 cURL feature. Detailed  verification (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/VERIFICATION.md) and  dependency records (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md) retain their own dates and limits.

   Scope became Snurpo in 1.4.2

The name and mascot changed; saved-data and integration identifiers remain compatible. Existing sessions, CA trust and MCP configuration do not need a branding migration.

Keep existing  scope.sqlite3 ,  scope-ca.pem ,  scope-ca-key.pem ,  .scope.json ,  SCOPE_   variables and  scope-mcp  configurations. The certificate subject can still say Scope. Do not rename or remove these files merely to update the branding.

Quit old Scope before opening Snurpo: both use the same local archive and ports. Keep a backup of important work before changing installations. Historical releases and checksums remain unchanged.

On macOS, the mascot menu offers   Show Snurpo   and   Quit Snurpo  . Quit uses the application's cleanup path. This does not introduce automatic startup or change capture settings.

Read the  migration reference (https://github.com/dalkedev/snurpo/blob/v1.5.0/docs/MIGRATING_TO_SNURPO.md) for all retained compatibility names.
